articles.title: The bees in the city: organizing China’s delivery workers in Ganzhou
articles.author: Tings Chak
articles.content_excerpt: At the entrance to Xingfuli, a residential compound in Ganzhou, Jiangxi province, a bulletin board displays the names, photographs, and phone numbers of the people responsible for managing the neighborhood. Though an ordinary bulletin board at first appearance, among the building representatives and Communist Party members is an unexpected name: Kang Jiafei, a food delivery worker who is also listed as a community “grid worker.” China has more than ten million food delivery workers, part of a rapidly growing global workforce whose lives are organized by algorithms, tight deadlines, and orders that take them across the city. articles.title: Trump-nominated WFP head has no credible plan to address fund crunch
articles.author: Pavan Kulkarni
articles.content_excerpt: “The number one thing we can do to reduce hunger in the world is to reduce the amount of conflict that is happening all around the world,” Luke Lindberg, the new executive director of the World Food Program (WFP), said in his first media address last week. Conflict is the main driver of hunger today, driving two-thirds of the acute food insecurity affecting 266 million people worldwide. “Conflict is a man-made situation. It is something that we can solve,” added Lindberg, who assumed office on October 26. Earlier this year, the WFP said that the “conflict in the Middle East” – a catch-all phrase for Israeli genocide in Gaza, US-Israeli war on Iran, and the Saudi war on Yemen – “is deepening this food crisis to an alarming degree,” warning of “record numbers of acute hunger if it continues.

articles.title: National Politics Will Never Be the Same: Juan González on How Latino Voters Remade the Political Map
articles.content_excerpt: The midterms saw a landslide of Latinos vote for Democrats. In Texas, California, Kansas and Colorado, Latinos who had voted for Republicans just two years ago voted for Democrats in large numbers, helping secure Democratic control of both the House and the Senate. Latino lawmakers will make up about a fifth of the Democratic majority in the House. And in an historic victory, the two most populous states in the country, California and Texas, will soon be led by Democratic Latino governors. “Texas has been suddenly transformed into a battleground state,” says Democracy Now! co-host Juan Gonzalez. “Texas has been the biggest and most important red state in the country for decades, and I’ve been predicting for years that it is the key link for achieving a realignment of national politics.”

articles.title: Hasan Piker Says Democrats Must Listen to Voter Anger That Put Them Back in Power
articles.content_excerpt: Tuesday was a historic night for progressive Democrats and, in particular, candidates backed by the Democratic Socialists of America. Six new DSA -endorsed candidates were elected to the House, and democratic socialists won mayoral races in Los Angeles, Washington, D.C., and Providence. “The Democratic Socialists of America had a phenomenal night, and this movement is only going to continue to grow,” says prominent leftist political commentator Hasan Piker. “Now, here’s the problem: Hakeem Jeffries and Chuck Schumer are two of the least popular politicians in the country right now, and there are demands to change the leadership in the Democratic Party to reflect the desires of this new coalition that was developed on November 3.”

articles.title: 1.6 million join general strike in France against austerity
articles.author: Ana Vračar
articles.content_excerpt: Following weeks of major mobilizations led by high school and university students , hundreds of thousands of people responded to a general strike call by French trade unions. On Thursday, November 5, over 200 events and at least 1,500 industrial action appeals brought the country to a standstill again. According to the General Confederation of Labor (CGT), roughly 1.6 million people took to the streets. The organization reported 350,000 people in Paris, 150,000 in Marseille, 120,000 in Bordeaux, and 100,000 in Lille, among others – despite authorities’ attempts to obstruct the day. Approximately 1.6 million people took part in protests across France on November 5, 2026. Author: Jaylen Strong Participants at strikes and rallies demanded concrete measures to address the cost-of-living crisis

articles.title: Jordanian security officer killed in stabbing attack in Amman
articles.author: Aseel Saleh
articles.content_excerpt: One Jordanian police officer was killed and another was injured in a stabbing attack outside the Sri Lankan embassy in Jordan’s capital, Amman, on Thursday, November 5. According to a statement issued by Jordan’s Public Security Directorate (PSD), the slain officer was identified as Corporal Jawad al-Salaytah. PSD also confirmed that the perpetrator was arrested by a police patrol that rushed into the site of the attack. Jordanian Government Communication Minister and Official Government Spokesperson Mohammad Momani said that the preliminary investigation revealed that the assault was a “cowardly terrorist attack.” Momani affirmed that “attacking security personnel while performing their duty is an assault on the prestige of the state and the rule of law, and an assault on every Jordanian.

articles.title: South Korea moves to join Iran War under US pressure
articles.author: Ju-Hyun Park
articles.content_excerpt: South Korea’s government has begun procedures to potentially join the US-Israeli war of aggression against Iran. On November 5, a vice-ministerial meeting affirmed a decision to expand the military capacities and operational area of the Cheonghae Unit, a blue-water naval force that has operated in the Gulf of Aden near the Red Sea as part of an “anti-piracy” mission since 2020. The revised mandate of the Cheonghae Unit would double its deployment area up to the waters of the Arabian Sea south of Duqm, Oman. This would place Republic of Korea (ROK) naval units on the fringes of the Gulf of Oman and the Strait of Hormuz – areas Iran has declared closed to foreign military vessels.
